prompt: In which quadrant is the cosine (across) NEGATIVE while the sine (up) is POSITIVE? Answer with the quadrant number.
hint: Negative across means LEFT of centre. Positive up means ABOVE centre.

hints.text: Negative across means LEFT of centre. Positive up means ABOVE centre.
Left and above is the top-left corner of the circle. Quadrants are numbered counter-clockwise starting from the top-right.

explanation: Cosine is the across number, so cosine is negative when you are to the LEFT of the centre.
Sine is the up number, so sine is positive when you are ABOVE the centre.
Left and above is the top-left corner — Quadrant $2$, covering $90^\circ$ to $180^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test one angle
steps: Try 120°, which lands in the top-left. Its point is about (−0.5, 0.87).
The across number is negative and the up number is positive. That angle is in Quadrant 2.

alternativeExplanations.title: Map the four corners
steps: Q1 top-right: across +, up +. Q2 top-left: across −, up +.
Q3 bottom-left: across −, up −. Q4 bottom-right: across +, up −. Only Q2 has minus-then-plus.
